body:
Global crypto markets closed Saturday, July 25, 2026 in clear defensive mode. Total market cap sits at $2.27 trillion, down 1.72% over the last 24 hours, with 24-hour volume registering $58.1 billion — a figure that reflects broad de-risking rather than panic. BTC dominance held at 56.5% as capital rotated toward the relative safety of the largest asset in the space, and ETH dominance slipped to 9.9%. The Fear & Greed Index printed 27 today versus 28 yesterday, both firmly in Fear territory, confirming that sentiment has not found a floor. There is no meaningful bounce bid evident in the structure of this session, and the macro backdrop is not lending traders any obvious reason to step in aggressively.

Bitcoin traded at $63,800, shedding 2.26% on the day and sitting essentially flat on the week at -0.22%, which tells you the selling has been steady rather than spike-driven. The hourly print of -0.26% suggests continuation pressure into the Saturday close rather than stabilization. The $63,800 handle is a key near-term battleground; failing to reclaim it with conviction keeps the door open to a test of lower demand zones that the data does not allow us to quantify precisely today, but which any participant watching the weekly chart through Q2 will recognize as meaningful. Michael Saylor and the Strategy team reportedly overhauled their bitcoin metrics as the bear market persists, according to CoinDesk — a notable signal that even the most committed institutional HODLers are adjusting their communication framework to the environment rather than doubling down on pure price optimism.

Ethereum dropped 1.88% to $1,851.8 on volume of $6.5 billion, and its 7-day figure of +0.44% is one of the few green weekly readings in the majors, suggesting relative resilience even as today's session was soft. That weekly outperformance looks increasingly fragile given the Cointelegraph report that Ethereum ETFs closed the week in the red, ending a 5-day inflow streak — institutional appetite clearly cooled heading into the weekend. Among the rest of the tracked universe, the divergences are worth noting. UNI was the worst performer in the 24-hour window at -4.77%, yet it remains the best weekly performer at +4.26%, meaning this session is trimming a sharp mid-week rally. ADA followed at -3.75% on the day with -2.64% on the week, and LINK dropped 3.02% despite carrying a thin positive weekly print of +0.26%. SOL at $73.71 fell 2.68% on the day and is -1.68% on the week, tracking broadly with the risk-off tone. DOT was the lone bright spot, up 0.12% over 24 hours though its 7-day print of -4.20% makes it a short-term bounce candidate rather than a leadership signal. AVAX is the other near-standout at -0.29% for the day, but -5.53% on the week exposes how much ground it has surrendered.

The macro picture driving this is a layered set of pressures rather than a single catalyst. On the regulatory front, a White House statement suggests Senate Democrats should accept the legislative compromises already won on Trump's crypto limits — CoinDesk framing that implies the stablecoin or broader digital asset bill is closer to resolution than markets have priced, but the uncertainty itself is a drag on positioning. The EU's move to include HTX exchange in Russian sanctions, per Cointelegraph, is another incremental tightening of the compliance perimeter for global crypto infrastructure. The House passage of a bill targeting insider trading by lawmakers adds to a broader legislative moment where Washington is actively reshaping the rules around finance and digital assets simultaneously. Separately, LMAX, the institutional crypto trading platform, is reportedly exploring a sale or IPO — a signal that infrastructure-layer players see a window in current valuations, or alternatively feel pressure to crystallize capital before conditions tighten further.

Heading into next week, the key variables are straightforward. Any legislative clarity on the U.S. crypto framework — particularly around the stablecoin debate referenced in the White House commentary — could act as a relief catalyst, especially for assets with direct regulatory exposure. The break or defense of $63,800 in BTC on meaningful volume is the clearest technical trigger to watch; a sustained move below it without a recovery bid would likely drag the total market cap through $2.2 trillion and accelerate the Fear & Greed reading toward the low 20s. On the ETH side, whether the ETF inflow streak resumes Monday open is a concrete near-term read on institutional conviction at current prices around $1,851.8. The $52.5 million raise by Sam Altman-backed World Network to combat AI deepfakes, per CoinDesk, is a reminder that venture capital is still deploying into the intersection of crypto and AI infrastructure regardless of spot price weakness — that narrative thread is one to monitor as a potential re-rating catalyst for the broader space if sentiment shifts. The risk to the bear case is a coordinated policy positive; the risk to any recovery is a macro shock that reinforces the current Fear regime.
